# Nemlig.com and James Shannon
Date: 2026-10-08 | Duration: 60.470001220703125m

## Summary
The team currently uses GrowthBook for feature flagging, AB Tasty for visual experiments, and PostHog for app session recordings, creating a complex mix of tools. GrowthBook was presented as a potential unified platform through open-source capabilities, BigQuery-native analytics, frequentist and Bayesian methods, an AI-powered Visual Editor, natural-language experiment design, bandit experiments, dashboards, APIs, CLI support, and Jira integrations. Existing SDKs and BigQuery pipelines across mobile, web, and server-side systems could support expansion, although cloud migration would require API-based flag transfers, data-connection changes, and front-end endpoint updates. The decision depends on feature parity, cost, usage-based pricing, segmentation capabilities, and enterprise support. GrowthBook Enterprise offers dedicated engineers, onboarding, training, and post-implementation assistance. Pricing discussions are planned after the Danish holiday, with a possible move to Enterprise by the end of October if terms are competitive.

## Keywords
feature flagging, A/B testing, GrowthBook, visual editor, BigQuery integration, experimentation analytics

## Action Items

**James Shannon**
Send session replay recordings examples to Nemlig team to demonstrate GrowthBook's web session replay capabilities (52:00)
Provide a detailed pricing overview including seat-based and usage-based models to Nemlig to support their evaluation of GrowthBook enterprise licensing (58:00)
Schedule a 15-minute commercial and pricing discussion meeting with Simon from Nemlig for early next week before James travels to Berlin (58:00)
Follow up via email with Nemlig team including meeting notes, support materials, session replay examples, and pricing information (59:00)

**Simon / Gitte Linding Thomsen**
Review GrowthBook pricing models and prepare for follow-up commercial discussion after the Danish holiday week (56:00)
Confirm the number of seats and users requiring access to GrowthBook enterprise platform, noting current usage of about 22 seats (58:00)
